data.name: Rufus
data.gender_notes: Rufus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Rufus means 'red-haired'. In Latin, it means 'rugged' or 'wolf'. In the New Testament, Rufus is mentioned as a companion of St. Paul. The name Rufus carries the meaning “Red-haired, rugged, or wolf” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rufus usually hope their child will grow to embody red-haired, rugged, or wolf and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength, endurance, and resilience.
data.etymology: Rufus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red-haired, rugged, or wolf.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rufus total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: רפוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רפוס - (Rufus) - פירוש: בן-אשר, ילד-אשר - השם רפוס נמצא במקרא 3 פעמים. הוא שמע מעיין (Acts 21:8), נכה (Acts 19:12), וכן (Mark 15:21). השם רפוס נחשב לחסר ספירה (קאנוניות)

in_greek.name: Ρουφός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ρουφός - Ρουφός - η προέλευση του ονόματος Ρουφός είναι ελληνική. Η λέξη Ρουφός σημαίνει Βασιλέας. Στη Βίβλο, ο Ρουφός είναι ο τρίτος στη σειρά από τους αξιωματούχους που ανέβασαν τον σταυρό (υπό την πνευματική κατευθύνσεις του Ιησού). Ο Ρουφός ήταν από την Ιερουσαλήμ. Ο Ρουφός είναι μια κοινή ονομασία στην Ελλάδα που σημαίνει βασιλιάς.

in_latin.name: Rufus
in_latin.long_meaning: Rufus - Rufus - origine a Graecia. Rufus meaning est fortis et magnus. In Biblia, Rufus erat tertius in serie auctoritatum qui crucem ascenderunt. Rufus erat de Ierusalem. Rufus nomen est commune in Graecia, significans regem.

in_english.name: Rufus
in_english.long_meaning: Rufus is a name with Hebrew and Greek origins. It is derived from the Hebrew word 'ruf,' meaning 'red-haired,' and the Greek word 'rufos,' meaning 'wise' and 'noble.' In the Bible, Rufus is mentioned as the third in a series of authorities who ascended the cross. He was from Jerusalem. The name Rufus is common in Greece, signifying a king or a noble person. In Christian tradition, the name Rufus symbolizes wisdom, nobility, and strength.

data.cultural_impact: Rufus was a common name among early Christians, particularly among converts from Rome and Greece. Its Greek and Latin origins add to its multicultural significance. It is also associated with St. Paul, one of Christianity's most influential figures.
data.spiritual_significance: Rufus can be seen as a symbol of ruggedness or endurance in faith. In the New Testament, Rufus is mentioned as a Paul's 'kinsman' and 'chosen in the Lord'. This suggests a deep commitment and loyalty to the faith. Additionally, the name carries a reminder of the redemptive nature of Christianity, which can transform even one with a seemingly insignificant or unassuming name like Rufus into someone significant in God's eyes.
